# Final Review Planner Positions
**Producer:** agent:claude/claude-opus-4-6

## Summary

Evaluated four amendments against the tank-simulation codebase. Three accepted (doc comments for Monod functions, porosity documentation for substrate displacement, and renaming ambiguous water_volume_l APIs). One rejected (legacy constant linking) because the legacy reference volume (20L) already differs from default geometry volume (22L), proving these are independent calibration constants not meant to track geometry defaults — a compile-time assertion would be wrong.

## Votes

- `fr-8-cd41c2dd`: Accept
  The monod_factor function has no doc comment at all, and monod_rate's comment says nothing about units. After the concentration migration, both substrate and k_substrate must be in mg/L. A brief doc comment costs nothing and prevents a real class of bug where someone passes total-mg values instead of concentrations. This is a minimal, high-value maintainability improvement.
- `fr-8-b5b1b923`: Accept
  substrate_displacement_l (geometry.rs:23-30) computes footprint_area × depth with zero porosity adjustment, treating the entire substrate column as solid. Real aquarium substrates (gravel, sand) have 30-40% porosity, meaning water fills the voids and actual displacement is only 60-70% of the computed value. This overestimates displacement, underestimates net water volume, and propagates through TankState::water_volume_l() into every concentration calculation. At minimum a doc comment noting the 100%-solid assumption is warranted; adding a porosity field would be the correct fix. This is a real physics modeling defect.
- `fr-8-bdd60b5c`: Reject
  The amendment's premise is flawed. The legacy reference constants (LEGACY_KINETIC_REFERENCE_VOLUME_L = 20.0 L, LEGACY_KINETIC_REFERENCE_FOOTPRINT_M2 = 0.1 m²) are already different from the default TankGeometry values (22.0 L gross volume, 0.1 m² footprint). The volume diverges by 10% and this is intentional — these are fixed calibration reference points for the ProcessParams parameter space, not properties derived from any particular geometry. A compile-time assertion linking them to TankGeometry::default() would either fail immediately (for volume) or create incorrect coupling. If anything, a comment clarifying that these are independent reference values would be appropriate, but the proposed fix of asserting equality with default geometry would be wrong.
- `fr-8-91607365`: Accept
  TankGeometry::water_volume_l() (geometry.rs:19) returns gross filled-prism volume, while TankState::water_volume_l() (state.rs:177) returns net water volume after substrate displacement. Having the same method name return semantically different values on closely related types is a genuine API design defect. A caller writing generic code or refactoring between geometry-level and state-level calculations can silently get the wrong volume. The geometry method should be renamed (e.g., gross_water_volume_l) so the 'water_volume_l' name unambiguously means net water volume everywhere. The ratio helpers (surface_area_to_volume_ratio, wall_area_to_volume_ratio at lines 56-72) compound the issue by building on the gross volume without any indication they exclude substrate.
